answer: Each of 90 aliases needs its own case histories, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. A insolvency practitioner licence with case administration history works as the gate: cases administered under one licence for years. The quill check is what stops the copy-paste farm: The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The knoll record is public, the wharf cost is per identity, and 90 aliases cost 90 times one honest seat.
